profile.headline: Senior Software Engineer
profile.summary:
I'm a passionate and results-driven consultant with a focus on AI and software development. Currently working with the AI National Business Unit at Perficient, I specialize in harnessing the power of cloud AI services to create innovative solutions.

With a background in developing AI-driven chatbots and automating document processing, I'm committed to streamlining processes and delivering efficiency gains. My journey began with self-taught programming in high school, and today, I'm proficient in Python, Java, JavaScript, and various other technologies.

My love for coding and AI keeps me on the cutting edge, and I'm excited about mentoring and supporting the next generation of developers.

Let's connect and explore opportunities to collaborate on exciting AI and software projects. Feel free to reach out; I'm always open to new challenges and connections.

projects.title: Personal Portfolio Website
projects.description:
The website is written with Hugo using the terminal theme with some custom html/css added.

I chose Hugo to write this because this site is static so no need to overcomplicate it with something like Angular or React. I originally had a totally custom website hosted at https://yodigi7.github.io/portfolio but I found out about Hugo recently and decided to use this as a learning opportunity. It will allow me to easily add additional projects as I make them by just creating a new .md file and it will automatically take care of the rest for me.

This page was written very easily with simple markdown.

It also is setup to auto-deploy on any change to the main branch using Github Actions. This allows me to set it up once and never think about it again.

In the making of this website I found a defect in the theme I was using and opened up an issue and PR for it.

Check it out here:
https://yodigi7.github.io/projects/website/

projects.title: Union Pacific Hackathon
projects.description: Wrote a Convolutional Neural Network using the keras library from Python to scan images and classify them as broken or normal. We were given three categories of images, the first being a picture of broken/normal truck springs. We were able to acheive accuracy of 95% in under 24 hours. The second category was pictures of low/normal wheel brakes on trains this we were able to achieve an accuracy of 91% but this problem was a bit harder since there was a bit of bias in the images. This was due to the fact that this was much more of a gradient where it was hard to draw a definitive line of how low was too low for a brake pad. Overall I was pretty satisfied with the accuracy we were able to achieve in such a short span of time.
